submissions.title: Charlotte could extend data center moratorium by nine months
submissions.excerpt: staff may ask the full council for an additional nine months to work on issues such as air pollution monitoring
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Charlotte's Transportation & Development committee voted Sept. 8, 2026 to advance a nine-month extension of the city's existing 150-day data center moratorium (which otherwise expires in early November) to the full council for a Sept. 14 vote. submissions.title: Gallatin city council advances 12-month data center moratorium for vote next week
submissions.excerpt: Gallatin City Councilors are expected to vote on a 12-month data center moratorium
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Gallatin, TN city council unanimously advanced a 12-month moratorium on new data center development on Sept. 8, 2026 (following a 5-2 Planning Commission recommendation), setting up a formal council vote the following week. Cited concerns: noise, odors, and strain on water/electric utilities near the city's existing large Meta campus; Gallatin currently has no restrictions on data centers beyond general zoning-location rules. City-wide restriction, not tied to a single tracked project. submissions.title: Eastport will hear petitions to ban an AI data center
submissions.excerpt: a ban on any data center bigger than 25,000 square feet
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Eastport, ME holds a public hearing Sept. 9, 2026 on two citizen-initiated ordinances prompted by DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC's FERC preliminary-permit application (filed for a 48-month study period) for a tidal-powered underwater AI data center off Eastport's Kendall Head area in the Western Passage. One ordinance is an outright ban on any data center over 25,000 sq ft; the other requires a citizen referendum for large developments and adds zoning rules. Eastport's city council previously passed a 180-day temporary ban. Not proposed as a new project here — the underlying proposal is still at the FERC preliminary-permit/exploratory stage with no disclosed MW or capex figures, and the finding is about the restriction rather than the project. submissions.title: Mount Pleasant to discuss adding restrictions on data centers
submissions.excerpt: Large-scale, what they call hyperscale data centers, are not going to be coming to Mount Pleasant, and this moratorium will make sure that doesn't happen.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Mount Pleasant, SC town council held first reading Sept. 8, 2026 of an ordinance imposing a 120-day moratorium on data-center-related zoning requests, following the Planning Commission's Aug. 31 recommendation. Purpose: study environmental, noise and water impacts and refine the town's data-center definition while excluding small existing business data facilities from the pause; the town currently has no zoning rules that specifically restrict data centers. Quote attributed to Mayor Will Haynie and reported near-identically across multiple Charleston-area outlets covering the same council session, so publisher attribution for the exact wording is uncertain.
